item.title: Solar Cold Hubs Cut Post-Harvest Fish Spoilage Along Lake Victoria Piers
item.description:
KISUMU — Before dawn along the timber jetties of Lake Victoria, wooden skiffs unload silver cyprinid and Nile perch directly beside humming white shipping containers topped with angled photovoltaic panels.

Inside the modular walk-in rooms, flake ice produced overnight keeps morning catches near freezing for forty-eight hours, removing the midday deadline that once forced small-boat crews to accept distressed prices on the shoreline.

Cooperative Ownership at the Pier

Managed by local landing-site committees, the solar cold hubs charge a per-kilogram chilling fee settled via mobile transfer rather than high-interest fuel loans for diesel generators.
